message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to bid on New York Avenue in this Monopoly auction.

I have $1137 and incomplete light blue, pink, and orange monopolies. The auction is at $350 with p2 as the only active bidder. I will likely drop out and hunt Tennessee and Virginia.

Bidding $351 to $400 still leaves enough cash to buy Virginia and Tennessee. p2 is likely raising the price to block an orange monopoly, not because they need it for a set.

I will bid once more, likely $375 or $400. If p2 raises again, I will drop out.

Bidding $450 would leave only $687. That is too thin to build houses on orange or pink. I should keep the bid closer to $375.

If I drop out, p2 will own New York Avenue for $350. That blocks my orange set until I buy it back at a premium. I cannot complete both the pink and orange monopolies immediately anyway.

I am now considering paying up to $450–$500 for New York Avenue. That would still leave enough cash to buy Virginia and Tennessee. Beyond $500 the remaining balance drops to about $297, which is too little to build meaningful houses. p2 has $1300 and is bidding purely to block me, so they may push the price higher than I am comfortable with.

I will bid $375. This is a measured step that continues the $25 increments without revealing my ceiling. p2 may match to $400, and I will face the final decision next turn.

I am reconsidering whether to bid $400 as a final offer. A round number might signal commitment and end the auction. I will keep the message calm and avoid showing desperation.
